summary: 3 findings adjudicated: 3 TRUE_DEFECT, 0 RED_HERRING, 0 UNCLEAR — all against current HEAD post-C2 runner fixes

verdicts.specQuote: Scope Pinning — reads confined to targetRoot via READ_SCOPE_VIOLATION; one-target law hunt ONLY inside targetRoot
verdicts.codeQuote: } catch (e) { void (e as Error).message; } // src/hydra/aether-tools.ts:67 inside makeCappedReadTool targetRoot check
verdicts.evidence: catch (e) { void (e as Error).message; } inside makeCappedReadTool targetRoot check silently swallows realResolve failure and falls through to fs.readFileSync without returning READ_SCOPE_VIOLATION
verdicts.divergence: C2-runner added isWithinRoot check but left fail-open on error; symlink loop or unreadable parent where realResolve throws bypasses confinement. Must fail-closed and return READ_SCOPE_VIOLATION with attempted path. Same pattern at grep 112-120.

verdicts.specQuote: runner-side tagging deterministic via DELETE-before-INSERT idempotent by canonical_id layerId:file:line with per-hunter tagsWritten in roster; LOUD log and continue on per-tag failure
verdicts.codeQuote: DELETE FROM typed_nodes WHERE canonical_id = ?; DELETE FROM typed_nodes WHERE canonical_id = ?; DELETE FROM typed_edges WHERE src_canonical = ?; INSERT INTO typed_nodes ... without BEGIN TRANSACTION
verdicts.evidence: DELETE FROM typed_nodes WHERE canonical_id = ? then delete for codeNodeId then delete typed_edges followed by separate INSERT INTO typed_nodes without BEGIN TRANSACTION/COMMIT in writeRunnerTag
verdicts.divergence: DELETE-before-INSERT not atomic — crash between deletes leaves typed_graph partially empty, breaking SRO correlations and runner-side tagging counts. Need WAL + transaction wrapper for atomic idempotent tag write.

verdicts.specQuote: ONE GRAPH LAW — extract ONCE, query N times with canonical file keys; graphify integration file keys canonical
verdicts.codeQuote: const id = v.file + ":" + v.line; if (!allFindings.some((f) => f.id === id))
verdicts.evidence: const id = v.file + ":" + v.line and if (!allFindings.some((f) => f.id === id)) uses raw file strings without path.resolve normalization before dedup
verdicts.divergence: fileToNodeIds built from absolute n.file (path.resolve) while lookup uses relative finding.file per template contract; no normalization on either side causes duplicate findingId for same file via relative vs absolute and inflates downstreamCount / false-empty blastRadius.
